title: Who was David?
summary: Samuel introduces David as a shepherd chosen and anointed as king, and 2 Samuel 7 makes God’s promise to David’s house a lasting thread in Israel’s story. Later biblical writers return to that royal promise in different ways, from Luke’s announcement about Jesus to the images in Acts and Revelation.
historical_context: The cited passages portray David’s anointing and rise, the promise concerning his house, and later biblical interpretations of Davidic kingship. They show how these texts remember and reuse David’s story, but this entry does not provide a full historical chronology or independent evidence about David’s reign.
canonical_context: In 1 Samuel 16, David is anointed after God directs Samuel to look beyond outward appearance; chapter 17 presents his encounter with Goliath. In 2 Samuel 7, God promises David a house and a continuing royal line. Psalm 2 uses royal sonship language, while Psalm 110 portrays a ruler addressed as lord and priest. Luke 1 applies David’s throne language to the child announced to Mary; Acts 2 argues from David’s words about the holy one; Revelation 5 combines the titles ‘Lion of Judah’ and ‘Root of David’ with the image of the slain Lamb. These later texts interpret Davidic hope in distinct literary settings.
literary_context: The references move from narrative to poetry and then to New Testament interpretation: Samuel narrates David’s anointing and the promise to his house; Psalms 2 and 110 use royal-poem language; Luke 1 announces a ruler in David’s line; Acts 2 gives a speech that reasons from David’s words; and Revelation 5 combines royal titles with a vision of the Lamb. Genre and setting shape what each passage says about David.
covenantal_significance: In 2 Samuel 7, David’s importance rests in God’s promise to establish his house, not in a claim that David is flawless. The promise becomes a basis for later hope: Luke 1 speaks of Jesus receiving David’s throne, and Acts 2 connects David’s words with its proclamation about Jesus. Revelation 5 uses Davidic titles within its vision of the Lamb. The links show development across the canon while preserving each text’s own claim.
canonical_role: Who was David? serves as a question-oriented anchor, connecting common reader language to related passages, themes, and CKL entries.

scripture_references.notes: lion of Judah and root of David

interpretive_notes.note: The listed passages do not portray David in only one way. Samuel narrates his selection and royal story; 2 Samuel 7 centers God’s promise to his house; the royal psalms use poetic language; and later texts interpret Davidic kingship in relation to Jesus. Identify which passage is making the claim before summarizing David as a model.

Later hope for a Davidic ruler draws on the promise in 2 Samuel 7. Luke 1 explicitly speaks of David’s throne, Acts 2 argues from David’s words, and Revelation 5 uses Davidic titles for the Lamb. These are later scriptural interpretations; they should not be treated as the only subject of every earlier David passage.
